Technical fixes

Eleven fixes on your site

Small things on your site that stop Google and AI reading it properly. We checked 32 pages on both sites. Each fix links to a free Google test you can run yourself.

  • Google dataLet Google see your star ratingThe thong shows 210 reviews, but the hidden code Google reads leaves them out, so no stars show in search. Same on the brief and speed rope.Rich Results Test ↗
  • Google dataLabel your FAQs as questions and answersIn the hidden code, so AI can lift your answers word for word.Rich Results Test ↗
  • Google dataTell Google what each page is aboutYour period, postpartum, perimenopause, pelvic-health and how-it-works pages only describe the company in their hidden code.Rich Results Test ↗
  • SpeedMake the home page fast on phonesMobile score 5 to 8, 43.8 MB to download, 7.3 to 8.4 s for the main image, and the layout jumps.PageSpeed, home ↗
  • SpeedSpeed up the thong pageMobile score 30 to 33 and 6.1 to 8.0 s for the main image.PageSpeed, thong ↗
  • HeadingsGive 8 pages a main headingHome, period, postpartum, perimenopause, pelvic health, how-it-works and the blog article have no main title in the code, which Google uses to work out the topic.The scan ↗
  • ImagesDescribe every imageGoogle and AI can't see pictures, they read a short description. Home is missing 10 of 32, how-it-works 11 of 13, about 5 of 7.The scan ↗
  • DuplicatesRetire the copy pagesA copy of the pelvic-health page is still live, and the brief's web address ends in "copy". Duplicates split Google's attention.The scan ↗
  • TitlesSay what you sell in the home titleThe name in the browser tab and in Google results is just "Double Undies®".The scan ↗
  • DescriptionsShorten the blurbs Google showsThe home page blurb is 241 characters and period underwear 320. Google cuts them off at about 160.The scan ↗
  • ContactAdd a one-tap email linkSomeone arriving from AI has no quick way to contact you.The scan ↗
Products described for GoogleCompany described on the home pageBlog article describedNo mixed-up page addressesNZ and Australian sites linked correctly

Profiles and listings

Help AI recognise you

Before AI recommends a brand, it checks that the brand looks the same everywhere: the same name, the same description, the same contact details. Right now there isn't much for it to check.

WorkingInstagram

@double_undies, 4,172 followers, linked from your site.

WorkingFacebook

@officialDU, 884 followers. Runs your ads.

Not set upApple Business Connect

Free, and open to online-only brands. No address needed. iPhones are 63% of phone browsing in Australia.

To checkGoogle store page

Google's free page for online shops: your logo, reviews, shipping and returns. No address needed.

To confirmTikTok

Not linked from your site. A handle exists with no following.

MissingReview sites

No ProductReview.com.au or Trustpilot page, so your reviews only live on your own site.

ThinDirectories

Only The Coach Club NZ and the Shop app list you.

OptionalGoogle Maps listing

Only for a place customers can visit, like a studio or showroom. Not needed for an online shop.

Don't want to show your address? You don't have to.
An online shop can do all of this without one. Google's map listing is only for places customers visit, and it doesn't allow a PO box or virtual office, so we'd skip it unless you open a studio or showroom. Apple's brand page and Google's store page both work with no address.

The fix, step by step

  1. Pick one short "about us" line, for example "Double Undies, designed in New Zealand, shipping to New Zealand and Australia", plus one email and your website.
  2. Put it on your site in the footer and on the contact page, with a link that opens an email in one tap.
  3. Copy it into every profile: Instagram, Facebook and TikTok say the same thing, word for word, and link back to your site.
  4. Add it to the hidden code on your site, with links to each profile, so Google knows they all belong to you.
  5. Set up the free brand pages: Apple Business Connect and your Google store page. Neither needs an address.
  6. Get reviews onto review sites: ProductReview.com.au and Trustpilot, so AI sees them outside your own site.

Sources: public profile reads 28 Oct, map and directory checks 31 Oct 2026 (evidence ↗). Rules: Google Business Profile guidelines ↗, Apple Business Connect ↗, Google store pages ↗.

Payment marks that match checkout

Checkout takes Afterpay and JCB, but the footer doesn't show them, and it shows Diners and Discover, which checkout doesn't list. We match the footer to what you actually take, once you confirm it in Shopify.
